title: Flair vs. Steamboat: The 1989 Trilogy
event_name: Chi-Town Rumble, Clash of the Champions VI and WrestleWar '89
wrestlers_involved: Ric Flair; Ricky Steamboat; Lou Thesz; Pat O'Connor; Terry Funk
description: Three NWA World Heavyweight Championship matches between February and May 1989, nominated together as a composite work of in-ring storytelling.
source_material: NWA Chi-Town Rumble pay-per-view (UIC Pavilion, Chicago, 20 February 1989); Clash of the Champions VI broadcast on TBS (Louisiana Superdome, New Orleans, 2 April 1989); WrestleWar '89 pay-per-view (Nashville, 7 May 1989); WWE.com interview with Flair and Steamboat
context_statement: Across three matches in eleven weeks, Flair and Steamboat set a standard for championship wrestling that is still used to judge long-form in-ring storytelling.
external_links: WWE.com: Flair and Steamboat on their famous trilogy (https://www.wwe.com/classics/wcw/ric-flair-ricky-steamboat-trilogy-interview); Chi-Town Rumble (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chi-Town_Rumble)

title: Bull Nakano vs. Aja Kong: The 1990 Cage Match
description: A no-referee steel cage match for the WWWA World Championship that showcased the intensity of women's wrestling in Japan at the start of the 1990s.
source_material: AJW Wrestlemarinepiad 1990 broadcast, Yokohama, 14 November 1990; Cagematch match database; retrospective reviews (Quebrada, The Indy Wrestling Experience)
context_statement: This cage match set a new standard for violence and drama in women's wrestling and helped define the joshi boom of the early 1990s.
external_links: Quebrada: Kanaami No Referee Death Match review (https://quebrada.net/columns/issue72/72d2.html); Retro Indy Rewatch: AJW Wrestlemarinepiad '90 (https://theindywrestlingexperience.com/2023/06/03/retro-indy-rewatch-5-ajw-wrestlemarinepiad-90-11-14-1990)

title: The Shockmaster's Debut
wrestlers_involved: Fred Ottman; Ric Flair; Sting; Davey Boy Smith; Ole Anderson
description: A planned dramatic reveal that collapsed when the debuting Shockmaster tripped through a wall on live television and lost his helmet.
source_material: WCW Clash of the Champions XXIV broadcast on TBS, 18 August 1993; WWE.com oral history "Shock and Awe"; interviews with Fred Ottman (Pro Wrestling Stories)
context_statement: The Shockmaster's trip turned a major reveal into one of wrestling's best-known blunders and remains a case study in how live production can undo a character in seconds.
external_links: WWE.com: Shock and Awe, the oral history of the Shockmaster incident (https://www.wwe.com/inside/shockmaster-incident-oral-history); Pro Wrestling Stories: Fred Ottman's side of the story (https://prowrestlingstories.com/interviews/the-shockmaster-fred-ottman/)

title: Mitsuharu Misawa vs. Toshiaki Kawada, 3 June 1994
description: A 35-minute Triple Crown defence at the Nippon Budokan that became the benchmark for the escalating, near-fall-driven style of 1990s All Japan Pro Wrestling.
source_material: AJPW Super Power Series broadcast, Nippon Budokan, Tokyo, 3 June 1994; Cagematch match database; contemporary and retrospective reviews (F4W Online, Fightful)
context_statement: Built on years of shared history between former partners, this match became the reference point for the "King's Road" style and is still cited as one of the greatest matches ever wrestled.
external_links: F4W Online: Daily Pro Wrestling History (06/03) (https://www.f4wonline.com/news/other-wrestling/daily-pro-wrestling-history-all-time-classic-misawa-vs-kawada-match); Mitsuharu Misawa (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsuharu_Misawa)

title: Guerrero & Barr vs. El Hijo del Santo & Octagón: Hair vs. Masks
wrestlers_involved: Eddie Guerrero; Art Barr; El Hijo del Santo; Octagón
description: A two-out-of-three-falls lucha de apuestas at When Worlds Collide that introduced many American viewers to the drama of lucha libre.
source_material: AAA/WCW When Worlds Collide pay-per-view broadcast, Los Angeles Memorial Sports Arena, 6 November 1994; Cagematch match database; Pro Wrestling Torch and F4W Online retrospectives
context_statement: Shown on American pay-per-view, this hair-versus-masks match brought lucha libre storytelling to a new audience and became the defining match of Los Gringos Locos.
external_links: AAA When Worlds Collide (Wikipedia) (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AAA_When_Worlds_Collide); Pro Wrestling Torch: Nov. 6 in history (https://www.pwtorch.com/artman2/publish/Torch_Today_2/article_74386.shtml)

title: King, from Tekken
wrestlers_involved: Seiichi Ishii (character designer); Tiger Mask (referenced); Fray Tormenta (referenced)
description: A jaguar-masked wrestler in Namco's Tekken whose look, moves and backstory pay direct homage to professional wrestling and lucha libre.
source_material: Tekken arcade game (Namco, Japanese release 9 December 1994); King (Tekken) and Tekken (video game) on Wikipedia; Tekkenpedia
context_statement: King brought a masked professional wrestler into one of the most successful fighting-game series, carrying wrestling's look and holds to a worldwide gaming audience for three decades.

title: The Montreal Screwjob
wrestlers_involved: Bret Hart; Shawn Michaels; Vince McMahon
description: The infamous real-life double-cross of Bret Hart by Vince McMahon at Survivor Series 1997, forever altering the landscape of professional wrestling.
source_material: WWF Survivor Series 1997 pay-per-view broadcast, Molson Centre, Montreal; Wrestling Observer Newsletter (November 17, 1997); Bret Hart, Hitman (2007); Wrestling with Shadows (1998)
context_statement: Vince McMahon's secret order to end the match against his champion's will became the most notorious finish in wrestling history, and its fallout gave rise to the Mr. McMahon character at the centre of the Attitude Era.

title: WrestleMania X-Seven: Stone Cold vs. The Rock
wrestlers_involved: Stone Cold Steve Austin; The Rock; Vince McMahon
description: The main event of WrestleMania X-Seven marking the end of the Attitude Era.
source_material: WWF WrestleMania X-Seven pay-per-view broadcast, Reliant Astrodome, Houston, Texas
context_statement: Stone Cold Steve Austin's heel turn alongside Mr. McMahon in the main event closed the Attitude Era's defining rivalry, days after the WWF's purchase of WCW.
